newsitem.title: USA: United Technologies gain aided by Pratt & Whitney.
newsitem.headline: United Technologies gain aided by Pratt & Whitney.

text.p: United Technologies Corp. said Wednesday that cost-cutting at its Pratt & Whitney aircraft engine unit helped the aerospace giant reap strong second-quarter earnings despite the effects of a strong dollar.

United Technologies earned $304 million, or $1.17 a share, in the second quarter, beating analysts' consensus estimate of $1.14 a share. This compared with earnings of $259 million, or 98 cents a share, for the same quarter last year.
Total revenues rose to $6.48 billion from $6.04 billion a year earlier. But a strong dollar cut revenues by $149 million and earnings per share by 4 cents, the company said.

United Technologies said the Pratt & Whitney aerospace division posted an operating profit of $210 million on revenues of $1.94 billion in the quarter, vs. a $160 million profit on $1.53 billion in revenues the year before.

The company attributed the 29 percent sales increase to higher after-market sales and higher commercial and military engine shipments. This, combined with cost cuts, helped the unit's profits grow 31 percent, the company added.

Operating profits at the company's Otis elevator unit edged up 3 percent to $113 million on flat revenues of $1.40 billion. Excluding currency fluctuations, the company said operating profits increased 11 percent and sales 5 percent.
The company said a strong dollar and a change in fiscal year accounting of its international subsidiaries largely offset the unit's improved profits in Europe and the Americas.

United Technologies' Carrier unit's operating profits rose 8 percent to $167 million on a 3 percent sales gain to $1.69 billion in the quarter. Profits grew 12 percent and revenues rose 6 percent on a constant currency basis, it said.

The company said the margin improvement in Carrier's North American residential and commercial businesses and the reporting change more than offset the currency impact, continued weakness in European sales, and the effects of a strike at a North American commercial products plant.

United Technologies automotive unit's operating profit plummeted 35 percent to $33 million on a 9 percent decrease in sales to $782 million. The Hartford, Conn.-based company attributed the drop to "continued performance issues" in its interior car business and strikes at customer plants.

Finally, the company's flight systems unit's operating profits rose 11 percent to $68 million as sales rose 9 percent sales to $702 million. The company ascribed the improvement to Hamilton Standard's double-digit revenue growth and the Sikorski helicopter division's continued strong performance.
United Technologies said it bought back 4.1 million shares for $302 million in the first half, compared with 3.5 million shares for $182 million in the first six months of 1996.
It added it paid a total of $101 million for acquisitions in the first half of this year.
United Technologies' stock fell 94 cents to $85.31 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
